analysis:
Both changed files are test-only Swift files: ProviderLifecycleTests.swift (head lines 220-242) and ProviderModelSwitchTests.swift (head lines ~189-229). No production source, trust-boundary code, crypto, attestation, or config handling changes in this batch, so no direct regression against the threat model (TB-002, TB-011, TB-012, A-018, T-053, T-059) is introduced.

The new lifecycle test shutdownDoesNotWaitForeverForAnUnloadThatNeverFinishes asserts that shutdownBeforeRegistration completes within 40s when a slot's native unload never finishes. It encodes a design where process exit releases the retained GLM5NextRetirement memory. That is availability-positive and relevant to T-028/T-029 (residual GPU memory, resource monopolisation). The test relies on helpers ModelLoadingSandbox, ModelLoadingFixtures, OneShotBoolContinuation, modelLoadingInstallSlot and modelLoadingMarkUnloading, which are outside the supplied evidence. The production fix that makes shutdown not wait is also not in this batch.

The new model-switch test theDaemonStateReportsTheFilterACommittedSwitchApplied checks that state.json reports enabled_models_at_start and enabled_models_at_last_switch. It also checks that a refused commit rolls enabled_models back to the old selection. This exercises the rollback path. It touches no sensitive data, and the state fields are model IDs that are already public through heartbeats. The patch excerpt was truncated, but the remaining displayed head lines match the base test patterns. The production code that writes these fields is not visible here. A later pass on the corresponding production change should check that state.json (owner-only file permissions) exposes only model IDs, and that the rollback is atomic with the concurrent config-edit protections.

No findings. The tests are low risk, but the corresponding production changes are not covered by this batch.
